title: BST260 Final Project Proposal
text: final project, propose two analyses using public health datasets encountered BST260. first investigate association body mass index (BMI) systolic blood pressure among adults NHANES. second describe patterns reported waterborne disease outbreaks using CDC dataset provided course package. analyses apply tools BST260 data cleaning, descriptive statistics, visualization, statistical modeling. present work two separate vignettes within finalproject R package publish reports pkgdown website.

what: Analysis 1: BMI and systolic blood pressure in NHANES
title: BST260 Final Project Proposal
text: use NHANES dataset NHANES R package, contains educational adaptation data 2009–2010 2011–2012 National Health Nutrition Examination Survey cycles. NHANES conducted National Center Health Statistics combines interviews physical examinations. document package version, original data source, variable definitions, steps used construct analysis sample. dataset adapted educational purposes, interpret results exploratory classroom analysis rather definitive national estimates. primary question : BMI associated average systolic blood pressure among adults aged 20 years older? also examine whether observed association changes accounting age sex. expect higher BMI associated higher systolic blood pressure, analysis evaluate pattern without assuming relationship causal. primary variables BMI, average systolic blood pressure (BPSysAve), age, sex variable provided dataset. first restrict sample adults aged 20 years older summarize missingness selected variables. report number participants included excluded step. Descriptive analyses include means, standard deviations, medians, interquartile ranges continuous variables, along counts percentages categorical variables. Histograms boxplots show variable distributions, scatterplot smooth curve describe relationship BMI systolic blood pressure. fit simple linear regression systolic blood pressure BMI, followed model adjusting age sex. report estimated differences systolic blood pressure per five-unit increase BMI. Model diagnostics assess linearity, unusual observations, residual patterns. uncertainty estimates interpreted light dataset’s educational resampling. cross-sectional analysis, establish temporal order causation. Blood pressure may also influenced medication use, diet, physical activity, factors included primary model. Missing data may affect composition analysis sample. future extension use original NHANES files appropriate survey methods obtain population-level estimates.

what: Analysis 2: Patterns in reported waterborne disease outbreaks
title: BST260 Final Project Proposal
text: use CDC waterborne illness dataset distributed waterborne finalproject package. analysis, review documentation original CDC source establish reporting period, unit observation, variable definitions, surveillance coverage. document dataset version, source URL, available years, cleaning aggregation steps. also check whether row represents individual outbreak aggregated surveillance record calculating summaries. primary question : number reported waterborne disease outbreaks associated illness burden vary available reporting years? secondary question whether outbreak frequency illness burden differ across reported etiologies water exposure categories, depending variables available. examine reporting year, outbreak counts, illness counts, available categories describing cause type water exposure. begin reviewing variable types, missing values, duplicate records, category labels. distinguish missing unknown values true zeros identify potentially incomplete reporting years. summarize reported outbreaks illnesses year. outbreak-level illness counts available, also describe distribution outbreak size using median, interquartile range, range. Line plots show annual patterns, bar charts compare categories. distinguish categories account many reported outbreaks associated large total number illnesses. descriptive comparisons; calculate population incidence rates without appropriate denominators. Surveillance data capture reported events may miss outbreaks detected reported. Differences across years categories may reflect surveillance practices, reporting delays, diagnostic changes well underlying disease patterns. Large outbreaks may dominate total illness counts. Therefore, describe patterns reported outbreaks without interpreting direct measures individual risk. future extension incorporate population exposure denominators investigate changes reporting completeness.
